tagline: Through Moccasin Gap and west to the Wilderness Road.
intro: Up from the Tennessee line, the road runs through Weber City and Moccasin Gap, a break in the mountains cut by Big Moccasin Creek, and on past Gate City, named in 1886 as the gateway to the West. It follows the Clinch River to Clinchport and then Stock Creek, where the railroad splits off north through the Natural Tunnel, and passes through the Devil's Racepath toward Duffield.
West of Jonesville US 58 becomes Wilderness Road, running through rolling hills and farmland along the slope of Poor Valley Ridge, by Rose Hill and Ewing, toward Cumberland Gap.

moments.title: Weber City
moments.text: A service-station owner put up a "Welcome to Weber City" sign as a joke borrowed from Amos 'n' Andy, and when the town incorporated in 1954 the joke became its name.

moments.title: Natural Tunnel State Park
moments.text: Groundwater and Stock Creek hollowed this cave through Purchase Ridge, up to 200 feet wide and big enough to carry the railroad.

moments.title: Wilderness Road State Park
moments.text: Inside the park a piece of Boone's 1775 road has been preserved, beside a rebuilt Martin's Station, once the only station along some 200 miles of the Wilderness Road.
